Cluster decks

39 decks, one per cluster, in study order: what raises your TEF speaking score most comes first.

How the order was set: level shown first (Section B is the longer task, and conceding, rebutting and pushing to a decision are the moves that read as B2/C1), then reuse (how many of the recorded model answers use the cluster), then cost (small must-haves like openings move up because they're quick wins).

Inside each deck the cards are ranked too, best first: reuse across exam prompts, B2/C1 level shown, one example of every move before a second one, short before long. Stop wherever you like; core is the point where the next cards add the least. Cards are grouped in tiers 1-4 (1 = drill first); inside a tier, cards of the same box (the same move) sit together, similar boxes next to each other, the best card of each box first: in a deck, pick T1-T4 at the top to study one tier, or all; reset only touches the tier you're in. New cards come in this order; in a deck, "reset in order" brings the ranking back after a shuffle.

What the tiers mean (two rankers judged every card: how often you can reuse it in any exam prompt, how much B2/C1 range it shows, whether it adds a move the higher cards don't already cover, and how short and learnable it is; a card's tier is the average of theirs, the better one when they were one apart)
T1 · drill first: essential. Reusable frames for almost any prompt, the deck's key moves shown cleanly. Drill these until they're automatic.
T2 · strong: high value. Second examples of key moves, or strong B2/C1 sentences that are a bit longer or more specific.
T3 · useful: good to know. Tied to one ad, longer, or overlapping with higher cards.
T4 · low priority: near-duplicates, long ad-specific stories, details you won't reuse. Skim them.
Sort:

Card front: the literal English, then what an American would say. Back: the French. In a deck, press e to edit a card, Esc when done. Progress and edits are saved in this browser only.
